comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Intel explicitly identifies AMD as a direct competitor in the full spectrum of CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators (Target, S001). AMD’s disclosure focuses on the financial outcome of this competition, reporting a 94% increase in Data Center net revenue driven by AMD EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPUs (AMD, S001-S002), which validates Intel's identification of AMD as a key rival in the data center and AI space.

sentences.text: Our competitors include hardware vendors such as AMD that compete with us across the full spectrum of CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, and other products; providers of GPU systems such as NVIDIA; companies developing their own custom silicon; and new entrants and incumbents developing ARM- and RISC-V-based products customized for specific data center workloads.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.
